brand.name: BMOSAN LABS
brand.tone: Precise, confident, and engineering-minded. Industrial in aesthetic, technical in tone — but with enough creative edge to never feel corporate. The brand communicates through restraint: tight color palette, bold typography, and no unnecessary ornamentation.
brand.audience: Developers, technical teams, enterprise clients, and creative professionals who value precision and results over polish and fluff.

motion.philosophy: Minimal and precise. Transitions are near-instant — they confirm actions, they don't perform. No decorative animation, no staggered reveals, no bounce or wobble. If motion is perceptible, it should feel mechanical, not organic.

buttons.primaryStyle: Black fill, cream text, mono font, uppercase, wide letter-spacing. Hover: background changes to signal orange.
buttons.secondaryStyle: Transparent background, black 2px border, black mono text. Hover: black fill, cream text.
buttons.tertiaryStyle: No background, no border. Mono text. Hover: 2px bottom border in signal orange, text color to signal orange.

cards.hoverEffect: Border strengthens from default to strong, faint sm shadow appears

inputs.focusRing: 2px border changes to primary (black), no ring/glow
inputs.errorStyle: Border changes to semantic error color, helper text appears below in error color with xs mono font

navigation.style: Numbered bracket pattern: [01] SERVICES [02] PROCESS. IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, wide letter-spacing. Logo left, links right. Minimal — no background color, no bottom border unless scrolled.

signatureElements.outlineText: Hero headings use a mix of filled and outlined (stroke-only) text in Barlow Condensed 800. Outlined text uses -webkit-text-stroke: 2px with transparent fill.
signatureElements.sectionLabels: Section labels use // prefix (code-comment style) in IBM Plex Mono, uppercase, signal orange color. Example: // WHAT WE DO
signatureElements.numberedSequences: Service items and process steps use zero-padded numbers (001, 002...) or two-digit numbers (01, 02...) in IBM Plex Mono, light neutral color.
signatureElements.diamondMarkers: List bullets and separators use a 6px diamond (rotated square) in signal orange instead of standard bullet points.
signatureElements.gridBackground: Pages use a subtle graph-paper grid pattern on the cream background using CSS linear-gradient. Grid lines are approximately rgba(180, 170, 155, 0.2) at 40px intervals.
signatureElements.arrows: CTAs use → (right arrow) as a suffix, not chevrons or icons.

dos: Always use CSS custom properties from the brand tokens — never hardcode values
Always import Barlow Condensed, IBM Plex Sans, and IBM Plex Mono from Google Fonts
Use the warm neutral scale — never use cool grays
Use all-caps Barlow Condensed for every heading
Use IBM Plex Mono for all labels, navigation, prices, and metadata
Use the // code-comment prefix for section labels
Use numbered bracket pattern [01] for navigation items
Use diamond markers (◆ or rotated squares) instead of bullet points
Use the graph-paper grid background on primary pages
Use signal orange sparingly — it's punctuation, not paint
Maintain generous whitespace — when in doubt, add more breathing room
Use semantic colors that feel warm and muted, consistent with the cream palette
Use → for CTA arrows, never chevrons or icon fonts
donts: Never use border-radius on buttons, cards, or containers — the brand is sharp and architectural
Never use pure black (#000000) or pure white (#FFFFFF) — use neutral-900 (#1A1A1A) and cream (#F2ECE4)
Never use cool-toned grays — all neutrals must be warm (cream-based)
Never use gradients anywhere — not on backgrounds, text, or UI elements
Never use more than the three core colors (cream, black, signal orange) plus neutrals and semantics
Never use sans-serif fonts other than the three specified families
Never use bouncy, springy, or playful animations — motion must feel mechanical and precise
Never use animation durations longer than 250ms
Never use thick shadows or dramatic elevation — depth is subtle at most
Never use emoji, rounded UI patterns, or anything that softens the industrial aesthetic
Never use signal orange for large filled areas — it's for small highlights, text emphasis, and markers only
Never center-align body text — left-align everything except single-line labels where centering is structural
